panels.title: Swarm init and service deployment
panels.body:
# Bootstrap swarm on first manager
docker swarm init --advertise-addr 192.168.1.10

# Get join token for workers / managers
docker swarm join-token worker
docker swarm join-token manager

# Deploy a replicated service
docker service create \
  --name web \
  --replicas 3 \
  --publish published=80,target=8080 \
  --update-parallelism 1 \
  --update-delay 10s \
  --update-order start-first \
  --rollback-parallelism 1 \
  --restart-condition on-failure \
  --constraint 'node.role==worker' \
  --limit-memory 512m \
  nginx:alpine

# Deploy a Compose stack to Swarm
docker stack deploy -c compose.prod.yaml myapp

# Force rolling update (e.g. after config change)
docker service update --force web

# Drain a node for maintenance
docker node update --availability drain node2

panels.title: Quorum and Raft gotchas
panels.body:
Swarm uses Raft distributed consensus. Manager count MUST be odd.
  1 manager: no HA, any restart loses scheduling.
  3 managers: tolerates 1 failure (quorum = 2).
  5 managers: tolerates 2 failures (quorum = 3).
  7+ managers: rarely worth it — more Raft overhead.

Lost quorum symptoms: 'Error response from daemon: rpc error: code = Unknown
desc = The swarm does not have a leader.' — no new tasks can be scheduled.
Recovery: docker swarm init --force-new-cluster on a surviving manager.

Routing mesh: publishing a port (mode=ingress) listens on 0.0.0.0:<port>
on EVERY node. Traffic is load-balanced to any healthy task regardless
of which node receives the request.

mode=host publishes only on nodes where a task is running. Use when
you need client IP preserved (no SNAT from routing mesh).

panels.title: update-order: start-first vs stop-first
pros: start-first: new task starts and passes health check BEFORE old task stops — zero downtime rolling deploy
start-first: immediate rollback if new task fails health check; old task never terminates
cons: stop-first (default): old task stops before new one starts — brief downtime but uses fewer resources during deploy
start-first requires headroom: you temporarily run replicas+parallelism tasks — nodes must have capacity
